Yingbo Fan

Multimodal intelligence for understanding, predicting, and acting in complex spaces.

I develop multimodal spatial intelligence that integrates visual perception, 3D geometry, language, and dynamics. My research focuses on efficient world models and grounded decision-making, with intelligent mining as a defining real-world frontier.

Research vision

Understand. Predict. Act.

My research asks a unified question: how can an intelligent system build a multimodal model of space, anticipate how that world will evolve, and act reliably within it? I approach this through representation, prediction, and deployment.

01

Understand

Multimodal Spatial Intelligence

Fuse panoramic vision, 3D geometry, language, and multi-source sensing into structured representations of complex environments.

02

Predict

Efficient World Models

Learn compact predictive representations of spatial dynamics for imagination, simulation, and planning under constrained computation.

03

Act

Intelligent Mining and Embodied Systems

Translate spatial understanding and predictive models into reliable decisions for intelligent mining and other embodied systems.

Current agenda

Research frontiers

All projects →
Multimodal Spatial IntelligenceFlagship research direction

CARVE-VLA

A vision-language-action framework that grounds multimodal reasoning in spatial structure, connecting visual observations, language, world state, and action.

World ModelsCore research direction

Lightweight World Models

A first-principles investigation of compact predictive models that preserve imagination and planning capability while reducing inference cost.

Geometry-Aware Spatial PerceptionResearch in progress

One Sphere, Many Charts

Group-Consistent Panoramic Depth from Frozen Foundation Models

A geometry-aware approach that transfers frozen foundation models to panoramic depth estimation through chart-based representations and group consistency.

Real-world frontier

Intelligent mining in complex physical worlds

Mines are large-scale, dynamic, and partially observable 3D environments where perception, prediction, and action must remain reliable under dust, low illumination, occlusion, and constrained computation. I use this frontier to study deployable multimodal intelligence, panoramic sensing, 3D digital twins, and decision support.
